messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-dequeue-backpressure spike detected for region=us-west-2. p99 stream write latency > 12s for the last 2m. Triggered paging to oncall @maya. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/streams/dequeue?svc=streaming-gateway

maya: acked — jumping on it. grabbing traces and proxy pools now.

ricardo: saw increased backlog on ingress-queue for gateway-primaries, client write buffers building. p95 up to 1.4s, p99s are the problematic ones.

ashley: possible correlated deploy 10:02 UTC to streaming-proxy (rolling). rolling deploy finished but had a few pods show OOMKilled earlier.

maya: running quick checks — tailing proxy logs for write errors and 502/504s.

maya: run: ```kubectl -n streaming get pods -l app=streaming-proxy -o wide```
maya: output: ```
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
streaming-proxy-5f8d6f9b6-2k7zq  2/2     Running   0          12m
streaming-proxy-5f8d6f9b6-7njr2  2/2     Running   1          12m
streaming-proxy-5f8d6f9b6-bkq4h  2/2     Running   0          12m
```

ricardo: the 1 restart aligns with OOM note. check /metrics for queue depth.

maya: metrics pulled: ```
# streaming_gateway_dequeue_queue_depth{instance="proxy-5f8d6f9b6-7njr2"} 348
# streaming_gateway_dequeue_queue_depth{instance="proxy-5f8d6f9b6-2k7zq"} 22
# streaming_gateway_dequeue_queue_depth{instance="proxy-5f8d6f9b6-bkq4h"} 18
```

maya: one proxy has huge backlog (7njr2). p99s originating from that pod. looks like uneven routing.

ashley: could be connection pooling between edge LB and backend proxies. any spike in client slow-consumers?

ops-bot: NOTE: customer-impact detected: ~0.6% of active streaming connections are experiencing >10s write delays; autoscale not triggered due to reserved capacity config. impacted customers: acme-inc, notebookai.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon and drain problematic proxy pod 7njr2; 2) ramp a temporary extra replica (scale to +2) for the proxy deployment; 3) enable proxy write-timeout fallback to 10s to free hung connections; 4) enable diagnostic sampling for slow streams.

ricardo: +1 for draining. add traffic-shed tag in ingress to nudge LB away from that instance before drain: ```kubectl annotate pod streaming-proxy-5f8d6f9b6-7njr2 traffic-shed=yes```

maya: running drain: ```kubectl -n streaming drain streaming-proxy-5f8d6f9b6-7njr2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data```

maya: drain started. LB shows connections moving off that pod (via envoy stats). backlog dropping: 348 -> 40 in ~18s.

ashley: scaling proxy deployment now: ```kubectl -n streaming scale deploy streaming-proxy --replicas=5``` (was 3)

ops-bot: Metric alert suppressed temporarily for this incident window by @maya to avoid noise.

ricardo: noticed client keepalive mismatch — some clients are sending very small TCP windows (mobile clients behind proxies). that causes slow consumers. we might need to enable server-side pacing or per-connection buffer limits.

maya: applied write-timeout tweak in config map (proxy.write_timeout_ms: 10000) and reloaded config on the fleet. watch for side effects.

maya: after changes, p99 dropped to ~3.2s across region in last 1m. p95 ~0.9s.

ashley: logs show now fewer stalled write attempts: ```
[2026-03-14T10:20:15Z] WARN write timeout for conn id=abc123 client=10.22.3.11
[2026-03-14T10:20:16Z] INFO connection closed, drained 120 queued chunks
```

ricardo: long-term follow-ups: - investigate allocator for uneven routing (sticky hash?), - add auto-scale rule that triggers on per-pod queue depth, - put slow-consumer detection earlier in ingress to reject bad clients.

maya: customer comms: ops-bot reported impacted customers. I'll draft a short note for SRE->CS with what happened and mitigation steps. can someone grab logs for acme-inc session IDs?

ashley: pulling logs and session traces now for acme-inc. found ~45 sessions showing prolonged chunk ACK delays. saving to S3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/1765432199/acme-sessions.log

maya: handoff — I'm staying on until stabilization. if it looks stable in 30m I'll hand to morning oncall @jordan. current status: mitigated, p99 reduced but still above baseline. action items: scale autoscale rule, add per-pod queue alert, investigate routing hash.

jordan: thanks — will pick up follow-ups and customer writeup after 0730 PDT. please add any notes to the incident doc: https://wiki.redwood.internal/incidents/1765432199

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated -> monitoring. duration so far: 00:18:31. channels opened: #incidents, #sre, #cs-highlight.

maya: one more note — enabled sampling for traces at 5% for streaming paths to capture slow consumer patterns. will revert after root cause triage.

ricardo: temporary measure, but we should be careful of trace cost. set TTL on archive logs.

maya: agreed. marking P0 -> P1 for postmortem and scheduling follow-up with infra and product to discuss routing and client backpressure mitigation.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: status=resolved at 1765432330 (automated after monitoring stable for 8m). final metrics: p95=0.87s, p99=1.9s (region=us-west-2).
